emerging_technology: NPU-accelerated on-device AI inference on edge-computing laptops
intended_application: Evaluate local transcription and draft summarization of clinician-dictated patient encounter notes on managed laptops; clinicians review every draft and enter the final note into the clinical record.
business_need: Reduce clinician documentation burden when connectivity is intermittent while protecting patient information.
users_stakeholders: Patients, clinicians, medical-records staff, clinic leadership, privacy officer and IT support
capabilities_constraints: Assume limited IT support, intermittent connectivity and a small replacement budget. Integration with the electronic health record, access controls, current legal and contractual requirements, model behavior and ongoing support are unverified. Start with synthetic cases only.
risk_consequence_context: Omitted medications, diagnoses or follow-up instructions could affect patient care; disclosure of patient information could cause serious privacy harm. No autonomous clinical decisions or direct record writes are contemplated.
management_question: Should the clinic evaluate local AI documentation on laptops in 2027, and which evidence and governance conditions must be met before any use with real patient information?
time_horizon: 2027 planning; synthetic-data evaluation before a separate decision on clinical use
additional_context: Hypothetical 2027 planning case prepared from the primary intake; all organization details and monitoring triggers are assumptions, not verified observations or forecasts. Technology is held constant across cases. Source seed: Microsoft, Copilot+ PCs developer guide, accessed 2026-11-16, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/ai/npu-devices. This vendor documentation describes supported NPU development; it does not independently establish performance, privacy or value for this organization. Seek multiple independent dated sources and verify current products, costs and claims at decision time; do not invent 2027 outcomes. Baseline: clinician-authored documentation and the clinic’s existing approved dictation or transcription process, if available. Complements: encrypted managed devices, access controls, validated offline operation, clinical workflow integration and privacy oversight. Compared with the primary case, documentation errors have clinical consequences and the clinic has less assumed support capacity; offline operation remains relevant. Clinical and privacy leads review monthly during any synthetic-data evaluation and after relevant policy or security changes; halt progression if privacy controls, clinical omission testing, an accountable support owner or required approvals are absent. Proposed thresholds for omission rates, review burden and availability must be agreed before any real-data test. Hype-sensitive claim: keeping inference on a laptop alone guarantees privacy and clinical reliability; verify actual data flows, device controls and task-specific performance.
